topic: Large-range XY flexure stage: size and dynamics of a 10 x 10 mm parallel-kinematic flexure bearing
citation: Awtar S, Parmar G. Design of a large range XY nanopositioning system. ASME J Mechanisms Robotics 2013;5(2):021008 (author PDF).
task_or_setup: Double-parallelogram flexure modules (DPFM), wire-EDM from 25 mm Al6061-T651; BEI Kimco LA24-20-000A voice coils; 5 kHz control
key_quantitative_findings: 10 mm x 10 mm range; beam length 47.5 mm, in-plane thickness 0.63 mm, height 25 mm; flexure bearing 255 x 255 mm, frame 385 x 385 mm; cross-axis coupling < 60 um, parasitic rotation < 100 urad; first natural frequency ~18 Hz; a mode at 1315 Hz falls to ~150 Hz at large displacement; voice coils 11.12 N/A, 111.2 N peak
limitations: Nanopositioning scale and priorities; aluminium flexures
relevance_to_design: Candidate 4 (planar parallel flexure stage) for a +-5-8 mm pen tip
transferability_reason: Scaling of flexure length with travel is general; the pen needs far less precision
design_implication: A planar double-parallelogram stage with +-5 mm travel needs ~50 mm beams: it cannot fit a 24 mm pen; only wire (NiTi) or gimbal flexures are compact enough
search_query: WebSearch: Awtar Parmar Design of a large range XY nanopositioning system 10 mm flexure

topic: Two-axis voice-coil tilt actuator: Optotune MR-15-30 fast steering mirror
citation: Optotune Switzerland AG. Datasheet MR-15-30 Rev. 3, fast steering mirror, 24.09.2025.
task_or_setup: Dual-axis voice-coil mirror with optical position feedback, MR-E-2/MR-E-3 drivers
key_quantitative_findings: Mechanical tilt +-25 deg per axis; mirror 15 mm; housing 30 mm diameter x 14.5 mm; 29.3 g; centre of rotation 1.3 mm behind the mirror surface; static motor constant 3 rad/A; resonance 11-13 Hz (x), 15-18 Hz (y); full-scale bandwidth 20 Hz (+-25 deg); small-signal bandwidth 300/400 Hz (+-0.1 deg); coil 11 ohm, 6 mH; 0.37 A RMS single axis (0.26 A both); 2 A peak for 10 ms; 1.5 W max mean power; repeatability 40 urad RMS
limitations: Optical product; no force constant in N; flexure/bearing details not given
relevance_to_design: A compact commercial 2-axis tilt actuator (a gimbal plus voice coils) at pen-like scale
transferability_reason: Same physics (2-axis moving-magnet tilt with a soft suspension); larger diameter than a pen bore
design_implication: +-25 deg with 20 Hz at full scale fits in 30 mm: a +-8-10 deg pen gimbal in a 20 mm bore with 80 Hz on small signals is plausible
search_query: WebSearch: Optotune MR-E-2 fast steering mirror datasheet mechanical tilt angle bandwidth

topic: Galvanometer (limited-angle moving-magnet) scanners: Cambridge Technology 62xxH series
citation: Cambridge Technology. 62xxH Series galvanometer scanners datasheet DS00003 R1 v4.
key_quantitative_findings: 6200H / 6210H: rotor inertia 0.013 / 0.018 g cm2; torque constant 1.20e4 / 2.79e4 dyne cm/A; coil 2.14 / 3.7 ohm; 52 / 109 uH; RMS current 2.3 / 2.4 A; peak 6 / 8 A; small-step response 130 / 100 us; weight 13.3 / 18 g; max scan angle 40 deg; 6200H housing about 12.7 mm diameter (drawing)
limitations: Optical scanners; torque rather than force; mirror loads
relevance_to_design: Candidate 4: a galvanometer-style rotary voice coil per axis
design_implication: Km of a 6210H = 2.79e-3 N m/A / sqrt(3.7 ohm) = 1.45e-3 N m/sqrt(W); at a 45 mm lever that is 0.032 N/sqrt(W) at the tip, about 3-10x below a flat-coil gimbal, for 36 g for two axes: rejected (CALC)

topic: Ultrasonic piezo linear motors (PI PILine P-661, U-164, U-264): speed, force, drive power
citation: Physik Instrumente (PI). Small ultrasonic motors and actuators catalogue pages (P-661, U-164, U-264, M-272).
key_quantitative_findings: P-661: 14 x 35 x 6 mm, 10 g, max velocity 500 mm/s, push/pull 2 N, holding 1.5 N powered down, 210 kHz, motor 120 V peak-peak, driver electronics 12 V and 5 W. U-164: 500 mm/s, 5 g acceleration, self-locking, push/pull to 4 N, 60 V RMS, driver up to 10 W. U-264: 250 mm/s, 7-15 N, 200 Vpp, 80-100 g
limitations: Driver power quoted for PI's drive boards, not an optimised pen driver
relevance_to_design: Candidate 4: piezo/ultrasonic tip drives
transferability_reason: Drive voltage and power are inherent to the principle
design_implication: Fast enough (500 mm/s), but 120 Vpp and 5-10 W of driver power per axis against a 0.08 W pen, and a self-locking friction drive cannot yield to the writer: rejected for the tip

topic: NdFeB N52 grade: remanence, coercivity, density, temperature coefficients
citation: Arnold Magnetic Technologies. N52 sintered neodymium-iron-boron magnets, datasheet (2015-10-21).
key_quantitative_findings: Br 1.42-1.48 T (nominal 1.45); HcB 836-1122 kA/m; HcJ >= 875 kA/m; (BH)max 390-422 kJ/m3; density 7.6 g/cm3; alpha(Br) -0.12 %/degC; alpha(HcJ) -0.62 %/degC; Curie 310 degC
limitations: Grade values; no demagnetisation check in the pen geometry here
relevance_to_design: Magnet remanence used by the gap-flux calculation (B_r 1.42 T low end)
design_implication: Use B_r 1.42 T for N52 (80 degC class) and the SH grades (~1.38 T, 150 degC) where the coil is warm

topic: Superelastic nitinol: recoverable strain and strength (large-deflection flexure material)
citation: Fort Wayne Metals. Superelastic Nitinol (materials page).
key_quantitative_findings: Up to 8 % tensile strain without significant permanent deformation after heat treatment; permanent set < 0.5 % after 8 %; UTS 1103-1378 MPa (straight annealed), 1379-1655 MPa (cold worked); upper plateau 448-758 MPa; lower plateau 48-483 MPa; active Af -10 to 22 degC
limitations: No elastic modulus or fatigue data on the page
relevance_to_design: Flexure option for a +-8-10 deg gimbal and for the XY wire stage
transferability_reason: Wire and strip forms exist; bending fatigue governs (AMF-142)
design_implication: Static stroke is not the limit for a NiTi gimbal; the cyclic strain amplitude is (AMF-142)

topic: Nitinol fatigue: strain-amplitude limit at 10^7 cycles
citation: Pelton AR, Schroeder V, Mitchell MR, Gong XY, Barney M, Robertson SW. Fatigue and durability of Nitinol stents. J Mech Behav Biomed Mater 2008;1(2):153-164.
task_or_setup: Diamond-shaped stent sub-components, mean strains -4 to +4 %, alternating 0.07-3 %, up to 1e7 cycles
key_quantitative_findings: 10^7-cycle fatigue strain-amplitude limit +-0.4 %; mean strain above about 1.5 % does not shorten life (increases it); the strain amplitude, not the mean, governs
limitations: Stent geometry and surface; bending of strips may differ
relevance_to_design: Fatigue allowable for NiTi flexures (0.4 % amplitude, safety factor 1.5 applied)
design_implication: Design NiTi gimbal strips to <= 0.27 % alternating strain at the usable travel
search_query: WebSearch: Pelton 2008 Fatigue and durability of Nitinol stents strain amplitude 0.4%

topic: 2-DOF Lorentz-force actuator (moving coil): force constants and force variation over a +-5 mm stroke
citation: Yang F, Zhao Y, Mu X, Zhang W, Jiang L, Yue H, Liu R. A novel 2-DOF Lorentz force actuator for the modular magnetic suspension platform. Sensors 2020;20(16):4365.
task_or_setup: Prototype 117 x 106 x 118 mm, 2.59 kg; FEM and measurement
key_quantitative_findings: Force coefficients 5.11 N/A (vertical) and 4.08 N/A (horizontal) measured (FEM 5.55 / 4.47, 9-10 % high); force varies 30.9 % (vertical) and 21.6 % (horizontal) over the full +-5 mm / +-10 deg motion; mean gap flux 0.33 T in 19-25 mm gaps; PID positioning 15 um
limitations: Large, moving-coil; different scale
relevance_to_design: Force-constant variation over a large 2-D stroke: the model's constant-Km assumption
transferability_reason: Same physics at a larger scale
design_implication: Expect 20-30 % Km variation over the stroke: the servo must linearise (Hall map) and the bench must map Km (EXP-N02)
search_query: WebSearch: two degree of freedom moving magnet Lorentz force tilt actuator axial air gap flat coils

topic: Constant-force springs: stock sizes, loads and rated cycle life
citation: Lee Spring. Constant Force Spring Series (catalogue pages 315-316).
key_quantitative_findings: Type 301 stainless strip; four life ranges 2500, 4000, 13000 and 25000 cycles; smallest stock part LCF 025 04 025S: 0.10 mm x 6.35 mm strip, ID 7.54 mm, 0.30 kg (2.9 N) load; rated load reached after an initial deflection of 1.25 x the diameter; one and a half wraps must remain on the drum
limitations: Stock loads are 20x the pen's 0.15 N; custom springs needed
relevance_to_design: The refill spring of architecture B slides 13.5 mm (Rev H) to 24-27 mm (+-6 mm travel)
transferability_reason: Strip-spring fatigue is inherent: each strip section flexes fully as it passes the drum
design_implication: Rated lives of 2.5-25 thousand cycles are far below the tremor-rate sliding of the refill (about 36 000 cycles per hour at 10 Hz): a constant-force strip spring is a fatigue risk; replace or test (EXP-N05)
search_query: WebSearch: constant force spring design data stainless small force catalogue life cycles

topic: Latching (self-holding) solenoid: zero-power hold
citation: Takano. Latching solenoids product page (TSB series).
key_quantitative_findings: Smallest listed TSB-0705: 16 x 16 x 35.7 mm, 5 mm stroke, holding force >= 3 N de-energised; switched by electrical pulses
limitations: Too large for a pen; pulse energy not given
relevance_to_design: Principle for the refill lift: a magnetic latch holds pen-up/pen-down with no power
transferability_reason: Principle transfers; the part does not
design_implication: Use a bistable magnetic latch (pulse to switch) for the refill lift; size a custom 0.5 mm version
search_query: WebSearch: miniature bistable latching linear actuator moving magnet datasheet stroke holding force zero power

topic: Handwriting kinematics: which stroke features are invariant (size vs duration)
citation: Teulings HL, Schomaker LRB. Invariant properties between stroke features in handwriting. Acta Psychol (Amst) 1993;82(1-3):69-88.
key_quantitative_findings: Vertical stroke size has higher signal-to-noise ratios and between-condition correlations than stroke duration or peak force; downstrokes more invariant than upstrokes; horizontal stroke size is not invariant; stroke durations show no between-stroke correlations
limitations: Abstract only
relevance_to_design: Autowrite plans letters in time freely: the writer's vertical size is the feature to keep
design_implication: The planner may retime strokes (durations are not invariant) but must keep letter heights; horizontal spacing can flex
search_query: WebSearch: Teulings Schomaker 1993 Invariant properties between stroke features in handwriting; PubMed efetch 8475777

topic: Handwriting kinematics: the speed-curvature (two-thirds) power law and its variability
citation: Zago M, Matic A, Flash T, Gomez-Marin A, Lacquaniti F. The speed-curvature power law of movements: a reappraisal. Exp Brain Res 2018;236:69-82 (on Lacquaniti, Terzuolo, Viviani 1983).
task_or_setup: Reappraisal with drawing data and Drosophila larvae
key_quantitative_findings: Angular speed proportional to curvature^(2/3) in planar drawing (Lacquaniti et al. 1983); the exponent varies with shape and environment (about 2/3 in air, 3/4 in water in one cited study); the law is not a statistical artefact
limitations: Law describes human timing; not a constraint on a machine
relevance_to_design: Speed profile of autowritten strokes (a human-like time law may read as more natural)
design_implication: The planner's constant-speed-limited timing ignores the 2/3 law; a human-like time law is an option for ink quality (not needed for legibility here)
search_query: WebSearch: Lacquaniti Terzuolo Viviani 1983 two-thirds power law

topic: Writing speed and line quality: objective speed benchmarks
citation: Dziedzic T, Yilmaz AS, Szafranska A. How fast is fluent handwriting? Forensic Sci Int 2026;383:112896.
task_or_setup: 35 hybrid ink/digitised samples written at 10-60 mm/s; experts rated line quality
key_quantitative_findings: Samples at average speeds 10-60 mm/s; poor line quality was most often assigned below 20 mm/s and good line quality dominated above 50 mm/s (chi-square significant; strong Spearman correlations)
limitations: Abstract only; forensic line-quality judgement
relevance_to_design: Drawing speed of autowrite (the planner draws at up to 45 mm/s)
transferability_reason: Ink line quality depends on speed for any pen
design_implication: Draw autowritten strokes at >= 20 mm/s where possible; slow drawing may look tremulous to readers (test in EXP-N07)
search_query: WebSearch: adult handwriting speed letters per minute study; PubMed efetch 41775119

topic: Handheld swept inkjet printer (a hand-swept device that lays text): PrinCube
citation: CNX Software. PrinCube said to be smallest handheld smartphone color-inkjet printer that prints on anything (crowdfunding), 2019-11-01.
key_quantitative_findings: Prints one line up to 14.29 mm (0.5625 in) tall as the user sweeps it; 900 mAh; about 6 h of continuous printing; tracking method not disclosed
limitations: Secondary account; crowdfunding claims; tracking undisclosed
relevance_to_design: The hand-sweeps, device-writes interaction exists commercially (inkjet, not a ballpoint)
transferability_reason: Inkjet with a wide head, no moving nib
design_implication: Autowrite is a known interaction; the pen's version draws with a nib within +-6 mm
search_query: WebSearch: handheld inkjet printer sweep over paper prints text as you move PrinCube specifications

topic: Near-field optical-flow sensor for a page sensor at a distance: PixArt PAA5100JE
citation: NZPRG (robots.org.nz). The PAA5100JE near optical flow sensor, 2021-07-09.
key_quantitative_findings: Working range 10-35 mm; tracking speed up to 45 in/s; output depends on the surface (author; no accuracy numbers)
limitations: Secondary; datasheet link returned an HTML page
relevance_to_design: A paper sensor that tolerates the pen's changing height and tilt
transferability_reason: Frame rate (242 fps elsewhere in search results) too low for a 1 kHz page sensor
design_implication: A far-field flow sensor is too slow for the 1 kHz, 2 ms page-sensor assumption; a mouse-class sensor needs a flat window near the paper (OPT-54)

topic: Actuator gap flux by magpylib with iron images; Rev H's lumped leakage factor recalibrated (this study)
citation: This study: nose2/magnetics.py, nose2/designs.revh_as_designed; results/nose2/nose2.json -> magnetics.
task_or_setup: magpylib 5.2 analytic cuboids, infinitely permeable planes by images (3 periods), 720 radial and 240 axial geometries
key_quantitative_findings: Rev H actuator gap flux: lumped formula (eta 0.55) 0.293 T vs images 0.118 T (eta 0.222); Km at the actuator 0.46 vs 0.19 N/sqrt(W), at the tip 0.348 vs 0.140 (Rev H states 0.47 and 0.355).  Surrogate vs magpylib: radial rel. RMS 6.6 % (max 27 %, 720 geometries), axial 5.9 % (max 22 %, 240).
limitations: No saturation, no finite iron, no FEM; image method is an upper bound
relevance_to_design: Force constant of every candidate and of Rev H
transferability_reason: Analytic magnets are exact; the iron model is idealised
design_implication: Measure Km on the Rev H bench before relying on 0.47 N/sqrt(W) (EXP-I05)

topic: Front-end closure (DEC-034) generalised to +-4-9 mm of tip travel (this study)
citation: This study: nose2/frontend.py (vectorised re-implementation of opt/inertial/front_end.py, checked to 1e-4 mm).
task_or_setup: Rules of FrontRules unchanged; 35-75 deg; every direction; z_p 30-80 mm
comparator: Rev H closure (R 6.75 mm, slide 13.5 mm)
key_quantitative_findings: At z_p 45 mm: nominal travel 3 -> 8 mm needs contact radius 6.75 -> 10.50 mm, refill slide 13.5 -> 31.8 mm, guaranteed minimum travel 2.75 -> 6.91 mm; checked against opt/inertial/front_end.check (max abs diff 0.0e+00).
limitations: Rigid geometry; no tolerance stack
relevance_to_design: Ring size, visibility and refill slide of a larger-travel nose
design_implication: Every mm of nominal travel costs about 0.75 mm of skid-ring contact radius and 3.7 mm of refill slide; the guaranteed travel is about 0.88-0.92 of the nominal

topic: Architecture B refill: a freely sliding refill follows ordinary pen lifts (this study)
citation: This study: CALC with opt/inertial/front_end.protrusion (docs/nose_v2.md section 6).
task_or_setup: Rev H ring (R 6.75 mm): extension available before the refill's forward stop
key_quantitative_findings: With the forward stop set for 35 deg, the ball stays on the paper for pen lifts up to 1.0 / 2.9 / 4.8 / 6.5 mm at 40 / 50 / 60 / 70 deg of tilt; the synthetic writers lift 1.5 mm between strokes
limitations: Assumes a free slide on a constant-force spring (Rev H text); friction ignored
relevance_to_design: Strokes would be joined by ink in Rev H and in any larger-travel B nose
design_implication: Architecture B needs a controlled refill (pen-up by the pen: brake and latch) for normal writing as well as for autowrite

topic: Travel needed for delayed ink (the ink trailing the hand by tau) (this study)
citation: This study: nose2/tasks.delayed_ink on synthetic aiguide writers (tuning), rescaled to LIT CON-20 speeds.
key_quantitative_findings: 50ms: p99 2.85 mm (synthetic speed), 3.81 mm (30.5 mm/s), 20 % of inked samples laid after the stroke's pen lift; 100ms: p99 4.53 mm (synthetic speed), 5.26 mm (30.5 mm/s), 39 % of inked samples laid after the stroke's pen lift; 150ms: p99 5.27 mm (synthetic speed), 7.73 mm (30.5 mm/s), 55 % of inked samples laid after the stroke's pen lift; 200ms: p99 6.69 mm (synthetic speed), 9.15 mm (30.5 mm/s), 54 % of inked samples laid after the stroke's pen lift
limitations: Synthetic writers (20-34 mm/s); no human acceptance data
relevance_to_design: Whether a +-6 mm nose can support delayed ink
design_implication: Delayed ink of 100 ms needs 4.5-5.3 mm; 39 % of its ink is laid after the hand lifts, so it needs the pen lift; whether writers accept trailing ink is untested (OPT-50-52)

topic: Position-correcting handheld tool, commercial: Shaper Origin correction range and retraction
citation: Shaper Tools. Complete Origin System product page; Help Center 'How does Shaper Origin work?'.
task_or_setup: Handheld CNC router with camera localisation and a motorised spindle stage
key_quantitative_findings: Auto-corrects within a 1/2 in (12.7 mm) range; automatically retracts when the user goes out of bounds; 43 mm digital depth of cut with automated touch-off; tool 6.75 kg; 'accurate to within 1/100th of an inch' of the intended path (claim)
limitations: Manufacturer claims; router, not a pen
relevance_to_design: The closest commercial analogue of autowrite: human coarse motion, device fine correction, retract when out of reach
transferability_reason: Same control split; different scale and load
design_implication: Autowrite should lift the refill (retract) when the text leaves the reach, as Origin retracts its cutter; the pen's axial DOF provides this
search_query: WebSearch: Shaper Origin specifications auto-correct range

topic: Cooperative handheld robots: intention prediction and user frustration when the tool disobeys
citation: Stolzenwald J, Mayol-Cuevas WW. Rebellion and obedience: the effects of intention prediction in cooperative handheld robots. arXiv:1903.08158 (2019).
task_or_setup: 6-DoF-tip handheld robot, block-assembly tasks with intention prediction and 'rebel' modes
key_quantitative_findings: Intention prediction 87.9 % (picking) and 93.3 % (placing) at zero anticipation; 71.6 % 500 ms before picking; 80.1 % 1500 ms before dropping; significantly higher frustration in rebel mode than follow-intention (p = .019); Bristol press release (2015): users preferred a fully autonomous tool and it cut completion time and workload
limitations: Pick-and-place, not writing; preprint
relevance_to_design: Human factors of a tool that moves on its own while held (autowrite mode)
design_implication: Autowrite must follow the user's sweep and never fight it; a mode the user turns on (docs/revJ_plan.md section 6)
search_query: WebSearch: Gregg-Smith Mayol-Cuevas cooperative handheld robot

topic: Letters presented to the hand by a mechanically moved stylus: size and speed readable
citation: Hasegawa K, Sakurai T, Makino Y, Shinoda H. Manual character transmission by presenting trajectories of 7mm-high letters in one second. arXiv:1503.07401 (2015).
task_or_setup: Stylus moved by a 2-D stepper stage with a solenoid for up/down; lower-case letters at 1 letter/s
comparator: 14 mm vs 7 mm letters, before/after 5 min training
key_quantitative_findings: 14 mm letters at 1 letter/s read 71.9 % at first, 91.3 % after 5 min training (SD 12.7 % -> 6.7 %); 7 mm letters still read 85.1 % (SD 8.2 %)
limitations: Reading by the hand, not ink
relevance_to_design: A device can move a held stylus through letters at about 1 letter/s; up/down by a solenoid (the axial DOF)
design_implication: Autowrite at 2-3 letters/s is faster than letter presentation to the hand; the stylus up/down solenoid is prior art for the refill lift
search_query: WebSearch: adult handwriting letter height writing speed (result: arXiv 1503.07401)

topic: Tip-mechanism candidates for +-5-8 mm, sized and optimised (this study)
citation: This study: nose2/designs.py, nose2/optimise.py (adjoint + CMA-ES); results/nose2/nose2.json -> optimise, recommended.
task_or_setup: Six candidates x travel 4-8 mm x mass weight x bore 22/24 mm; duty calibrated on HW1
key_quantitative_findings: Recommended: gimbal_sphere in a 24 mm handle, guaranteed travel 6.0 mm (nominal 6.49 mm at 50 deg), Km at the tip 0.099 N/sqrt(W), moving mass at the tip 2.1 g, coil loss 0.182 W autowriting with 1 mm tremor (0.164 W stabilising only), added mass 19.3 g.  Rev H in the same models: Km at the tip 0.140 N/sqrt(W), 2.75 mm guaranteed.

topic: Autowrite in model HW1: the pen draws a known text while the hand sweeps (this study)
citation: This study: nose2/autowrite.py, nose2/evaluate.py; results/nose2/nose2.json -> test.
task_or_setup: HW1 (handwriting/, read-only) with a causal page-sensor + IMU estimator, look-ahead DP planner, axial pen-lift; test writers 0-5, seeds 200-203
comparator: the clean target (recogniser ceiling); no axial DOF; Rev H travel
key_quantitative_findings: 2.5 mm letters, no tremor: ink error 29 um, letters read 99.2 % (ceiling 100.0 %), words (app) 100 %, 3.66 letters/s, coil 0.089 W; 2.5 mm, 1 mm tremor: ink error 36 um, letters read 99.2 % (ceiling 100.0 %), words (app) 100 %, 3.66 letters/s, coil 0.166 W; 2.5 mm, 2 mm tremor: ink error 60 um, letters read 98.3 % (ceiling 100.0 %), words (app) 98 %, 3.66 letters/s, coil 0.376 W; 3.0 mm, no tremor: ink error 28 um, letters read 99.2 % (ceiling 100.0 %), words (app) 100 %, 3.08 letters/s, coil 0.088 W; no pen lift, 2.5 mm, no tremor: ink error 59 um, letters read 99.2 % (ceiling 100.0 %), words (app) 100 %, 3.66 letters/s, coil 0.119 W

relevance_to_design: Whether 'the pen writes for you' works inside the nose's reach

topic: Perceived latency while inking with a stylus (delayed digital ink)
citation: Annett M, Ng A, Dietz P, Bischof WF, Gupta A. How low should we go? Understanding the perception of latency while inking. Proc Graphics Interface 2014:167-174.
task_or_setup: High Performance Stylus System (1 ms rendering, 7 ms inking baseline); JND by PEST; line, word 'party', star; ink offset 6.5 / 65 mm; hand hidden
key_quantitative_findings: JND 53 ms line drawing (range 31-76), 50 ms writing 'party' (32-87), 61 ms star (21-82); median 53 ms; hand and stylus visible: median 59 ms (33-104); hidden: 97 ms (59-105), p < 0.005; cites prior work: 1 vs 2 ms discriminable while dragging, 7 vs 40 ms not while scribbling
limitations: Digital ink on a projected surface; perception, not acceptance
relevance_to_design: Delayed ink (100-200 ms) trails the hand: will writers notice?
transferability_reason: Visual latency perception transfers; paper ink differs
design_implication: 100-200 ms of ink delay is 2-4x the perception threshold with the hand visible: writers will see it; acceptance is untested (EXP-N08)
search_query: WebSearch: Annett Ng How low should we go perception of latency while inking

topic: Delayed visual feedback during handwriting: errors grow with delay
citation: Tamada T. Effects of delayed visual feedback on handwriting. Japanese Psychological Research 1995;37(2):103-109.
task_or_setup: English words written with visual feedback delayed 0, 33, 67, 100, 133, 167, 267, 500 ms
key_quantitative_findings: Writing error rate increased with delay; frequent addition errors (strokes duplicated, e.g. 'feeling' -> 'feeeling'); visual monitoring indispensable for repeating a set of strokes
limitations: Abstract only; whole visual scene delayed (TV), not only the ink
relevance_to_design: Delayed ink
transferability_reason: Delayed-ink pens show the hand in real time; only the ink lags
design_implication: Delayed ink could disturb repeated strokes (m, n, u, w); test before adopting (EXP-N08)
search_query: WebSearch: delayed visual feedback handwriting study delay 100 ms 200 ms

topic: Delayed visual feedback on handwriting and tapping: insertion errors and larger letters
citation: Morikiyo Y, Matsushima T. Effects of delayed visual feedback on motor control performance. Percept Mot Skills 1990;70(1):111-114.
task_or_setup: Reciprocal tapping and handwriting of Kanji and English words with delays 200-1000 ms
key_quantitative_findings: Handwriting performance showed a large decrement with increasing delay; most frequent errors: insertion of line elements or letter duplication; written letters grew larger with longer delays
limitations: Abstract only; whole visual feedback delayed
relevance_to_design: Delayed ink
design_implication: Treat delayed ink as a risk to fluency and letter size; measure with the hand visible and only the ink delayed

topic: 3-D Hall sensor for a larger nose travel: TI TMAG5170
citation: Texas Instruments. TMAG5170 high-precision 3D linear Hall-effect sensor with SPI, datasheet (2021).
key_quantitative_findings: Ranges +-25/50/100 mT (A1; A2 to +-300 mT); 20 kSPS single axis; sensitivity linearity error +-0.1 % (XY); XY noise 140 uT RMS typical at CONV_AVG 000 (24 uT at 101), Z 61 / 11 uT; offset +-200 uT max (25/50 mT); 3.4 mA active; 2.3-5.5 V; -40 to 150 degC
limitations: SPI; field map calibration needed at large travel
relevance_to_design: Nose position sensing over +-6 mm (a larger field swing than Rev H's +-3 mm)
design_implication: Use the +-50 mT range and a per-unit field map; noise as the TMAG5273 (OPT-45)
search_query: WebSearch: TMAG5170 3D Hall sensor datasheet measurement range sample rate noise

topic: Mouse-class optical navigation sensor for the page sensor: PixArt PMW3360
citation: PixArt Imaging. PMW3360DM-T2QU product datasheet, optical gaming navigation sensor (rev 1.50, 2016).
key_quantitative_findings: Up to 12000 frames/s; 250 in/s (6.35 m/s) typical; 50 g; up to 12000 cpi (about 2.1 um per count); resolution error 1 % typical; lens reference plane 2.2-2.6 mm (2.4 nominal) from the surface; lift cut-off 2 or 3 mm; 16.3-18.6 mA
limitations: Needs a flat lens parallel to the surface at 2.4 mm; the pen tilts 35-75 deg
relevance_to_design: Autowrite depends on a fast page sensor (1 kHz, 2 ms assumed)
transferability_reason: Frame rate and resolution meet the assumption; the mounting does not (tilt)
design_implication: Mount the sensor in a gimballed foot on the skid ring or accept a tilted optical path; EXP-N06 must confirm 1 kHz / 2 ms / <= 5 um on paper at 35-75 deg

topic: Guided tool with a coarse and a fine positioning system (Shaper Tools)
citation: Shaper Tools Inc (inventors Hebenstreit JJ, Moyer IE, Blum JE, Rivers AR). Systems, methods and apparatus for guided tools with multiple positioning systems. US 2021/0034032 A1, published 2021-02-04; granted 2023-03-21 (as displayed).
key_quantitative_findings: Claim 1: a first (fine) positioning system with a frame moving a working member over a small region; a second (coarse) system positioning the frame over a large region with less accuracy; a controller moving the second system to keep target points within the first system's region. Description: fine range 0.5 in (about 12.7 mm), accuracy +-0.01 in; coarse +-0.25 in; z-position by force sensing on the tool base. Status displayed: active to 2039-01-29
limitations: Summary tool read; attorney must read the granted claims
relevance_to_design: Candidate 3 (coarse-fine) and the autowrite split (hand = coarse, nose = fine)
design_implication: FTO item for autowrite: in the pen the coarse system is the human hand (not a motorised stage); record this for the attorney
search_query: WebSearch: Shaper Tools patent Systems methods and apparatus for guided tools

topic: Plotter pen lift by solenoid: high-speed pen up/down (CalComp)
citation: California Computer Products Inc (inventors Klassen FE, Miller DG). High speed pen actuating mechanism. US 3,340,541 A, filed 1965-01-18, published 1967-09-05. Expired.
key_quantitative_findings: Solenoid plunger with an annular pole piece lifts the pen; a pen-pressure spring of about 7 g presses it down; axial movement 0.020-0.025 in (0.5-0.64 mm) at 40-50 Z pulses per second; air gap < 0.050 in for fast response
limitations: Plotter, not handheld
relevance_to_design: Candidate 5: the pen's own pen-up/down
design_implication: A 0.5 mm refill lift at >= 40 switches/s is established (expired) art; the pen needs a low-power latch variant
search_query: WebSearch: patent pen plotter pen lift solenoid mechanism fast pen up down

topic: Voice-coil actuator for angular movements with arc-shaped magnets (constant gap under rotation) (Thorlabs)
citation: Thorlabs GmbH (inventors Boehme T, Krause E, Baumhackl SMF). Voice coil actuator for angular movements. US 11,960,143 B2, granted 2024-04-16; priority 2019-11-13.
key_quantitative_findings: Two plates on a pivot joint; a pair of voice-coil actuators per axis at equal and opposite distances; each magnet structure conforms to an arc centred on the rotation axis; segmented coils switched by magnet position; +-8 deg per axis; net force on the pivot about zero at all tilts; active, expires 2042-12-11 (as displayed)
limitations: Summary read; tip-tilt mirror mounts
relevance_to_design: The constant-gap (spherical) actuator variant gimbal_sphere
design_implication: FTO item if the spherical-gap actuator is chosen; the recommended flat-coil pole-pair design avoids arc magnets
search_query: WebSearch: patent two-axis tilt actuator moving magnet coils fast steering mirror flexure gimbal voice coil

topic: Dual-axis flexure gimbal with four voice coils for tip-tilt (Raytheon)
citation: Raytheon Co (inventors Gallagher JM, Ready R, Fierro E). Dual-axis flexure gimbal device. US 11,441,598 B2, granted 2022-09-13; priority 2018-12-20.
key_quantitative_findings: Claim 1: a flexure spring-mass body with two sections joined by a diaphragm with a central aperture, and a cylindrical flexure unit in the aperture with four slots forming flexures for x/y rotation while restricting other motions; four voice coils tip/tilt the moving section; 'a few degrees' (e.g. 0.5 deg for image stabilisation); active, expires 2040-12-19 (as displayed)
limitations: Summary read; optical use
relevance_to_design: Rev H and Rev J noses (flexure gimbal + four voice coils)
transferability_reason: Structure similar; the claim's slotted-cylinder flexure differs from cross-strip flexures
design_implication: Add to the Rev H FTO list with PAT-12 and PAT-08; the attorney should compare the claim's slotted cylinder and diaphragm with the cross-strip gimbal

topic: Hand-held printer that prints while moved freehand, tracked by optical navigation sensors (HP)
citation: Hewlett-Packard Co (inventor Yamada N). Handy printer system. US 5,927,872 A, granted 1999-07-27; priority 1997-08-08. Expired.
key_quantitative_findings: Optical sensors image the print medium's surface features to generate navigation data; a navigation processor maps image data to positions and deposits ink segments as the user moves the device freely (non-linear motion); four sensors, 32 x 64 pixel arrays with a 24 x 56 reference frame; 600 dpi; about 50 us sampling at 0.45 m/s
limitations: Inkjet; expired
relevance_to_design: Prior art for autowrite (device lays text where it is while the hand sweeps, using surface-feature navigation)
design_implication: Expired prior art supporting novelty/FTO arguments for autowrite with page-sensor navigation
